name: A year of books of a Macao trading and consulting company that files no periodic return

contacts.name: Rua da Felicidade Trading Company Limited

documents.why: A domestic sale of services, MO-S-NA: the not-subject code posts the line's base and nothing else — no tax line, no declaration box.
A domestic sale of goods, MO-S-NA on the goods side too: the code draws no distinction the way a real turnover tax would between what is sold.

An export of goods to a customer outside Macao: MO-S-NA applies exactly as it does to V2's domestic sale, because a territory with no turnover tax draws no export/domestic line to begin with. The invoice is in patacas; Hong Kong dollars circulate widely in Macao, but the pack models no second-currency mechanics (Código Comercial, article 46(2), only requires a foreign-currency value to be stated also in patacas).
A credit note against V2, a partial return of goods — the golden's sale-side credit note.
A second domestic service sale, to spread the scenario across more than one month and leave an invoice a part-payment settles only partly.
A third domestic goods sale, settled by nothing in this scenario — an open receivable the trial balance has to carry at the year end.
A domestic purchase of trading inventory, MO-P-NA: the purchase side of the not-subject code, posting the base and nothing to recover.
A recurring domestic expense, office rent, paid in full by E3 — the golden's matched payment on the purchase side.

An import of raw materials from a supplier outside Macao: no import tax posts, because Macao levies no general tax on goods crossing its border (the consumption tax reaches only spirits and tobacco), and MO-P-NA reads the same on an import as on a domestic purchase.
A credit note against P1, a partial return of defective stock — the golden's purchase-side credit note, beside CN1 on the sale side.

A purchase of a fixed asset, computer equipment, booked straight to the balance sheet rather than to an expense account — proof MO-P-NA posts its base wherever the document line's own account sends it, and nowhere of its own choosing.
A recurring administrative purchase, the premium of the business insurance policy, booked on the insurance account.
A recurring administrative purchase, accounting fees: a Group A taxpayer's complementary tax declaration (Form M/1) has to be signed by the responsible accountant, so the fee is a regular cost.

payments.why: An inbound payment that exactly settles V1 — the golden's matched payment on the sale side.
An inbound part-payment on account, matched to nothing — the golden's unmatched payment and the open item a return computed from matchings has to survive.
An outbound payment that exactly settles P2 — the matched payment on the purchase side.
An outbound part-payment on account to a supplier, matched to nothing — the unmatched payment on the purchase side.
